channel.description: Personally scored news, world affairs, opinion/analysis & foreign affairs, business & finance, and San Diego/local articles curated by news-filter

item.title: Cybersecurity experts outline steps to guard against PHP vulnerability
item.description:
Source: Business Insider Original headline: Here's how to protect your information from the PHP flaw, according to cybersecurity pros
OpenAI researchers uncovered two critical vulnerabilities in PHP, a programming language used on 70% of websites. The flaws could allow hackers to access personal data stored on affected systems. The National Security Administration warned that exploits could steal sensitive data or disrupt services. Madeline Lawrence of Aikido Security emphasized that many users rely on systems vulnerable to these flaws, noting Cloudflare reported millions of exploitation attempts. PHP has released updates to mitigate the risks, but individual users are advised to adopt security measures. Cybersecurity experts recommend using password managers, enabling two-factor authentication, checking bank security advisories, and ensuring software updates. Peter Wildeford suggested using tools like 1Password and YubiKey for stronger protection. Lawrence cautioned against panic, urging users to act on data breach notifications rather than closing accounts unnecessarily.

item.title: PHP Security Flaws Threaten 70% of Websites
item.description:
Source: NPR Topics: News Original headline: Hacking attempts rise after flaws found in program affecting 70 percent of websites
Security flaws in PHP, a programming language used by 70% of websites, were discovered by Wiz Research using OpenAI technology. The vulnerabilities could allow attackers to take control of servers, steal data, and deface websites. Cybersecurity firms and governments worldwide are urging immediate action to patch the flaws. The U.S. National Security Agency and the U.K.'s National Cyber Security Center warned of heightened risks, while Japan's Prime Minister urged urgent fixes. Dozens of government sites in the U.K., France, and China were temporarily taken offline. Matthew Prince of CloudFlare reported tens of thousands of hacking attempts within minutes of the flaw's disclosure. Wiz Research noted the vulnerabilities had existed for decades but were only recently exploitable due to AI's ability to simplify the complex attack chain. The firm emphasized the severity, calling it one of the most impactful vulnerabilities in recent memory.

item.title: Quest Diagnostics reports cyber breach affecting patient records
item.description:
Source: San Diego Union-Tribune Original headline: Quest Diagnostics reports cyber breach affecting ‘certain patient records’
Quest Diagnostics reported a cyber breach affecting its Quanum Lab Services Manager system, which handles test orders and results. The company discovered unauthorized access on Wednesday and notified federal law enforcement. It estimates 'certain patient records' were accessed, but the full scope remains under investigation. The New Jersey-based company is collaborating with cybersecurity experts to address the breach. Quest Diagnostics has faced previous data breaches: 34,000 patients were impacted in 2016, and 11.9 million patients were affected in 2019 via a separate hack. Cyberattacks are increasing across industries, with recent incidents disrupting sectors like retail and education. While global efforts focus on addressing PHP vulnerabilities affecting 70% of websites, Quest Diagnostics confirmed its breach is unrelated to the PHP issue.

item.title: Sundar Pichai says Google is far from the ‘end state’ of self-improving AI
item.description:
Source: Business Insider
Google CEO Sundar Pichai said self-improving AI remains distant, stating researchers are using AI agents to assist in model development but are not yet at the 'end state' of recursive self-improvement. Pichai described the process as involving 'RSI loops' alongside human researchers, with AI helping automate parts of model-building. He noted progress is expected to continue into next year. Google cofounder Sergey Brin emphasized the company's Flash and Gemini models are demonstrating AI's ability to aid its own development, calling it 'starting to get onto that RSI treadmill.' A Gladstone AI report suggested most experts believe RSI could begin within three to 12 months, possibly sooner without government action. Pichai also highlighted AI's role in coding, citing that 75% of new Google code is AI-generated, with a one-third reduction in code rollbacks. He noted AI tools are improving code quality and productivity, and are used to track model development and internal discussions.

item.title: US Treasury Proposes New Rules to Restrict High-Tech Investments in Adversaries
item.description:
Source: San Diego Union-Tribune Original headline: US Treasury proposes a rule to crack down on high-tech investments in China, other adversaries
The U.S. Treasury Department proposed new rules to restrict American investments in high-tech sectors of countries deemed adversarial, including China, Russia, North Korea, Cuba, Iran, and others. The rule expands restrictions to cover hypersonic systems, supercomputing, biotechnology, and artificial intelligence, using the term 'superintelligence' as preferred by former President Trump. The measure implements the 2025 Comprehensive Outbound Investment National Security Act, which targets technologies that could bolster military capabilities. Investments over $50,000 are subject to review, excluding many financial investments. Experts noted the rule signals Washington's focus on tracking capital flows and managing risks. Treasury will accept public comments before finalizing the rule. A recent $200,000 fine against a U.S. company for failing to report a $92,500 investment in a Chinese AI firm highlights enforcement efforts. The move continues U.S.-China tech rivalry, which includes export restrictions and tariffs, with tensions recently eased but not resolved.

item.title: Mortgage Rates Stay Above 7% as Housing Market Stalls
item.description:
Source: NerdWallet Original headline: Mortgage Rates Remain Above 7% in a Stalled Housing Market
Mortgage rates remained above 7% as of October 22, with the 30-year fixed-rate average dropping eight basis points to 7.26% APR. Rates have stayed above 7% for about a month, similar to spring 2024 and longer than fall 2023. Forecasters predict rates will stay elevated into 2025. Home buyers face challenges from high rates, prices, and limited inventory. Pending home sales in September fell 7.3% month-over-month and 11.3% year-over-year, with all four regional markets showing declines. Sellers also struggle, as selling a home often means buying a new one at higher prices and rates. Builders report low sentiment due to rising costs and reduced demand. New construction is slowing, with building permits and starts down in September. Experts suggest lower rates and more affordable housing could help, but current conditions make buying or selling difficult for all parties.

item.title: Artificial Reef Sounds Boost Larval Settlement, Study Finds
item.description:
Source: San Diego Union-Tribune Original headline: La Jolla-based study looks at role of artificial acoustic sounds on rebuilding reefs
Scripps Institution of Oceanography at UC San Diego released two studies showing that underwater acoustic enrichment—playing sounds from healthy reefs—can influence fish and coral larval behavior, aiding reef restoration. Researchers used sounds from O‘ahu’s reefs, broadcasted via underwater speakers at artificial reefs off Moku o Loʻe, Hawaii, during 2023 and 2024 spawning events. Fish larvae responded more dramatically to sound playback, with larger numbers aggregating near structures, while coral larvae showed attraction to reef-associated sounds. Study author Océane Boulais noted lunar phases amplified natural soundscapes, and artificial reefs, not necessarily living ones, could attract larvae. Aaron Thode highlighted synthetic chemical cues likely play a role in settlement. The research also raised questions about specific sound components and how larvae detect them. Future work will explore sound’s role in kelp forests. The studies suggest acoustic enrichment could be a tool for reef rebuilding, though mechanisms remain unclear.

item.title: U.S. orders some diplomats to leave Saudi Arabia amid Houthi attacks
item.description:
Source: Washington Post - World
The U.S. State Department ordered nonemergency diplomats and their families to leave Saudi Arabia after Houthi militants escalated attacks on Saudi infrastructure and airports. State Department spokesman Tommy Pigott cited recent Houthi strikes, including attacks on civilian airports and critical infrastructure, causing civilian casualties and travel disruptions. Saudi Arabia’s aviation authority confirmed a second death in an attack on King Fahd International Airport in Dammam, with eight others injured. Houthi spokesman Nasr al-Din Amer claimed drone and missile strikes over the past 48 hours, including the Dammam attack. The group also claimed responsibility for a 2023 attack on Riyadh’s airport that killed 13, including an American. Analyst Adam Baron noted Houthi efforts to sustain pressure on Saudi Arabia. The conflict follows a ceasefire breakdown in Yemen, with Houthi advances along the Red Sea coast and Saudi counterstrikes. The U.S. has limited military involvement, while Britain announced sending fighter jets to protect Saudi infrastructure. The Houthis previously warned airlines against using Saudi airspace and have targeted oil facilities near the UAE border.

item.title: PHP Security Flaw Forces Global System Updates
item.description:
Source: BBC News Original headline: Race to update services' computer systems after cyber-security flaw found
PHP security flaws caused global system disruptions as developers rushed to patch critical vulnerabilities. Websites worldwide were taken offline after the PHP development team disclosed 'severe' flaws that could allow remote code execution if unpatched. The UK government temporarily shut down 32 services and four partially, citing precautionary measures. Tech Minister Baroness Lloyd of Effra attributed the outages to security updates. No successful attacks were reported, but experts warned the impact could take months to materialize. The National Cyber Security Centre called the event 'unprecedented,' noting no breaches were detected. Cybersecurity firm Wiz identified the flaws, now dubbed 'php2shell,' affecting 70% of global websites. Cloudflare reported a surge in attack attempts, with millions of probes detected post-announcement. While some services like Wikipedia and Finland's government resumed operations, others like Orange suspended access. Security professionals emphasized the urgency, with Matt Hull of NCC Group warning of a shrinking response window and potential burnout among teams. The PHP Foundation warned attackers could exploit the flaw under the right conditions, prompting widespread patching efforts.

item.title: Sri Lanka's Iconic Elephant Death Sparks Habitat Concerns
item.description:
Source: Deutsche Welle Original headline: Sri Lanka: Death of iconic elephant raises habitat concerns
An iconic male elephant known as Kavantissa, considered the tallest living male in Sri Lanka, died after a gunshot wound to his leg. The 45-year-old elephant, weighing 5.5 tons, was found limping in late September and died on October 16 despite veterinary care. Sri Lanka records the highest number of elephant deaths annually and the second-highest number of human fatalities from human-elephant conflict. Since 2019, an average of 370 elephants and 125 humans have died yearly in such incidents. Habitat loss, agricultural expansion, and fragmented corridors drive the conflict, with elephants raiding farmland to meet their 150 kg daily food needs. Ravi Corea of the Sri Lanka Wildlife Conservation Society attributes the crisis to shrinking forests, rural population growth, and land conversion for agriculture. The government's 2020 action plan faces calls for stronger habitat protection. Community initiatives like Project Orange Elephant and the EleFriendly bus service aim to reduce conflicts. Experts stress the need for scientifically informed land-use planning, corridor protection, and compensation for affected families to ensure coexistence.

item.title: Airbnb Bans Mandatory Checkout Chores for Guests
item.description:
Source: San Diego Union-Tribune Original headline: Airbnb guests no longer have to wash the dishes or strip the beds at checkout
Airbnb guests will no longer be required to perform tasks like washing dishes, stripping beds, or taking out trash under new rules effective Nov. 20. Hosts may only ask for "reasonable" checkout requests, such as leaving dishes in the sink or sorting recyclables, but cannot demand chores typically handled by professional cleaners. Exceptions may apply in specific situations, like requiring trash in animal-proof containers in bear-prone areas. Hosts must now disclose all house rules in a designated listing section, prohibiting additional requirements via messages or signs. The policy aims to address recurring disputes over cleaning fees and differing expectations between hosts and guests. Airbnb standardized house rules into seven categories, including overnight guests, quiet hours, and pet policies. The changes follow CEO Brian Chesky’s 2023 acknowledgment of uncertainty for guests due to varied rental conditions. He emphasized the need for transparency, stating guests should "know exactly what they’re going to get before they book."

item.title: Mortgage Rates Rise Slightly Amid Bond Market Shifts
item.description:
Source: NerdWallet Original headline: Mortgage Rates Today, Thursday, October 22: A Little Higher
Mortgage rates rose slightly to 7.28% APR on Thursday, up four basis points from the previous day but seven basis points lower than a week ago. The increase is driven by bond market shifts, with investors moving into Treasuries amid concerns about AI profits and potential renewed hostilities in Iran. Bond yields, which influence mortgage rates, have risen as inflation fears persist, partly due to higher costs for AI infrastructure and geopolitical tensions. While tech sector doubts initially eased bond buying, Iran-related risks have reignited inflation concerns, pushing yields higher. Mortgage rates are tied to 10-year Treasury yields, so bond market movements directly affect borrowing costs. Investors selling bonds at lower prices have increased yields, contributing to the rate rise. Despite the uptick, rates remain below levels seen earlier in the fall. Homeowners are advised to consider refinancing if current rates are at least 0.5 to 0.75 percentage points lower than their existing rate, though most may not qualify. Lenders adjust rates daily based on market conditions, so locking in a rate is recommended if a deal is secured.

item.title: United Airlines Flight 1157 Faces Severe Turbulence, Injures 4 Attendants
item.description:
Source: LA Times Original headline: Severe turbulence hits L.A.-bound flight from Hawaii, injuring 4 flight attendants
United Airlines Flight 1157 from Hawaii to Los Angeles experienced severe turbulence during descent, injuring four flight attendants. The Boeing 777 dropped 3,675 feet in one minute during the final 20 minutes of the flight, according to FlightAware. The plane departed Honolulu’s Daniel K. Inouye International Airport at 1 p.m. and landed safely around 9 p.m. Wednesday. United Airlines confirmed four attendants were treated by medical personnel, with one hospitalized. No passengers were injured. San Diego resident Marly Wadlington described the sudden drop and shaking, while Coral Pena reported hearing a bang before the turbulence. The aircraft remained on the tarmac for at least 30 minutes after landing, with injured crew members staying onboard.

item.title: Corgi Hires Investment Bankers on Commission-Only Basis
item.description:
Source: Business Insider Original headline: Buzzy insurtech Corgi is hiring experienced investment bankers. The catch? The pay is commission-only.
Corgi, a $5 billion insurtech firm, is hiring a Managing Director for investment banking with a commission-only pay structure. The job posting seeks experienced professionals with over five years of experience, established client relationships, and a track record in transaction origination and execution. Unlike traditional investment banking roles, which typically include base salaries and performance-based bonuses, Corgi's position offers no base salary, with compensation tied to collected transaction fees. Industry data shows investment banking managing directors earned a median of $1.1 million in 2025, with bonuses comprising over two-thirds of total compensation. Corgi's aggressive fundraising—$266 million in 2024 and $431 million since 2014—and its vision as an AI financial infrastructure company may attract ambitious bankers. The role focuses on connecting startup founders with private equity investors, aligning with Corgi's strategy to serve startups by facilitating business sales. The company, founded by Emily Yuan and Nico Laqua in 2024, also operates cafés as a marketing tool for founders. It did not respond to requests for comment on the hiring or strategic plans.

item.title: Expedia Uses AI Agent Mike Davis to Train Sales Team
item.description:
Source: San Diego Union-Tribune Original headline: Expedia hired Mike Davis to train its sales team. But he’s not ready to do the job himself.
Expedia Group hired Mike Davis, an AI agent developed by Seismic, to train its sales team. Davis, designed to mimic a skilled sales manager, provides real-time feedback and simulates challenging scenarios for reps. During a demo, Expedia sales managers reported the AI’s realism and noted a 5% increase in deal wins. Seismic’s tools, including Deal Agent, automate administrative tasks and analyze sales data to identify risks. At IBM, meeting prep time dropped from hours to minutes, while Royal London Asset Management saved 10,000 hours annually using AI bots. Seismic CEO Rob Tarkoff emphasized AI’s role in shifting job tasks rather than replacing workers, noting agents focus on structured tasks but lack human empathy. Tarkoff acknowledged AI’s potential to displace jobs but argued it creates new roles for engineers and strategists. The company’s AI agents, like Derek, have been targeted in social media trolling, showcasing their ability to mimic human-like responses. Tarkoff downplayed concerns about job loss, stating AI’s impact mirrors past technological shifts without reducing the number of sellers.

item.title: Nevis to Restore Alexander Hamilton Museum with US Funds
item.description:
Source: San Diego Union-Tribune Original headline: Tiny Caribbean island of Nevis to restore Alexander Hamilton museum with US funds
The Caribbean island of Nevis has received $245,000 in U.S. funds to restore the Hamilton House museum, where Alexander Hamilton is believed to have lived as a child. The 17th-century Georgian stone building, originally constructed around 1680, was destroyed by an earthquake in 1840 and last restored in 1983. Nevis Premier Mark Brantley praised the funding, noting the site’s historical importance and its role in showcasing Nevis’s contribution to U.S. history. The museum, now housing documents from Hamilton’s early years and exhibits on other Caribbean figures, requires ongoing repairs due to weather damage. Brantley emphasized Hamilton’s legacy as a symbol of what a small island nation can achieve, stating the restoration benefits both Nevis and the U.S. by inspiring future generations through the founding father’s story.

item.title: Over 40 Companies Lay Off Staff in 2026 Amid AI and Economic Shifts
item.description:
Source: Business Insider Original headline: Companies laying off staff this year include Meta, Amazon, and Visa — see the list
Over 40 companies have laid off employees in 2026, with more than 100 filing WARN notices for future cuts. Amazon eliminated 16,000 roles globally in January, citing efforts to reduce bureaucracy, following prior cuts. Angi cut 350 jobs to optimize operations, saving $70M–$80M annually. Atlassian reduced 10% of its workforce, or 1,600 employees, as it invests in AI, with CEO Mike Cannon-Brookes stating AI changes skill demands but does not replace people. Barclays plans to cut 5,000 roles, targeting support functions, while Cloudflare laid off 20% of its workforce, over 1,100 employees, citing AI-driven restructuring. Coinbase cut 14% of staff, with CEO Brian Armstrong linking layoffs to AI efficiency gains. Dell reduced its workforce by 10% for the third consecutive year. eBay and Epic Games also announced cuts, with Epic citing declining game engagement. The World Economic Forum survey noted 41% of companies expect workforce reductions due to AI, with AI-related jobs projected to double by 2030. Companies cited cost savings, efficiency, and strategic realignment as primary reasons for layoffs.

item.title: University of San Diego President to Retire After Boosting Enrollment and Reputation
item.description:
Source: San Diego Union-Tribune Original headline: University of San Diego president to retire after greatly improving the school’s fortunes
James Harris III, president of the University of San Diego, will retire after improving the school’s reputation in science, engineering, and business while boosting enrollment and strengthening Catholic ties. Harris, who served since 2015, will step down next year following a successor search. He cited advancing the university’s mission as his reason for leaving, crediting staff and values-driven leadership for elevating USD’s national standing. Harris, known for his approachable style, led efforts to increase enrollment from 8,251 to 10,023. Philanthropy under his leadership included a $50 million donation from Don Knauss for business education and a $75 million gift from Darlene Marcos Shiley to expand STEM programs. Construction of a biomedical engineering facility and housing for students is underway. During the 2020 pandemic, Harris guided the campus through remote learning and logistical challenges, teaching some classes and planning to deliver diplomas in multiple cities. He told the Union-Tribune, 'This is a really hard moment. I really miss the students.'

item.title: Typhoon Champi Causes Widespread Disruption in East Asia
item.description:
Source: BBC News, Deutsche Welle Original headline: Typhoon Champi Disrupts East Asia with Record Storm Activity and Evacuations
Typhoon Champi has caused widespread disruption across East Asia, leading to flight cancellations, school closures, and mass evacuations. The storm, intensified by El Niño, is expected to bring heavy rain, strong winds, and large waves to Taiwan, Japan, and the Philippines. At least one death and 171 injuries have been reported in Taiwan, with over 1,300 people evacuated and 1,000 displaced. Japan's Okinawa experienced power outages affecting 8,400 households, and more than 160 flights were canceled. The storm, which peaked with wind gusts of 191km/h, is forecast to pass near Taiwan's northeastern coast before heading toward Japan's eastern waters. Authorities warn that any deviation from its path could result in a direct hit, with Taiwan's weather agency noting the storm's wide radius could impact most of the island. Japan recorded its 30th typhoon of the year, the first time since 2013. The UN described the El Niño phase as 'heading off the charts,' with potential long-term impacts. Taiwan suspended work and classes in 22 counties, closed its stock exchange, and kept military and rescue teams on standby. Heavy rainfall is expected to continue through Saturday, raising flood risks.

item.title: Magnitude 7 Earthquake in Tibet Kills 16, Injures 65
item.description:
Source: San Diego Union-Tribune, BBC News, Deutsche Welle Original headline: Magnitude 7 Earthquake in Tibet Kills at Least 16, Injures Dozens
A magnitude 7.0 earthquake struck Tibet on Thursday night, killing at least 16 people and injuring 65, according to Chinese state media. The quake, which occurred at 10:33 p.m. local time, had its epicenter 119 miles east-northeast of Nagqu and a shallow depth of 10 miles, causing widespread destruction. At least 339 residential buildings and 20 livestock sheds collapsed, displacing over 12,400 people. Search and rescue operations continued with over 1,600 residents and supplies including 1,000 prefabricated housing units, 3,000 tents, and winter clothing. Communication and power lines were disrupted, with partial restoration reported by Friday morning. National Highway 317 was closed due to rockfalls, allowing only emergency vehicles. Intermittent snowfall over the next three days complicates rescue efforts. The quake is the strongest in the region in five years and the most powerful to strike China since January 2024. Survivors described violent shaking, with one resident fleeing barefoot and another comparing the tremors to 'several hundred yaks running past us.' Authorities declared an emergency, with Premier Li Qiang urging urgent rescue efforts and President Xi Jinping ordering all-out search and rescue. The Ministry of Emergency Management dispatched a working group, allocating 50 million yuan for relief. Rescue teams, including military and drones, address challenges from high-altitude terrain and aftershocks. The region, prone to seismic activity, has faced similar disasters, including a 6.2 magnitude quake in Gansu in 2023 and floods and landslides in Tibet and Nepal less than two months ago, which killed at least 1,400 people.
item.source: San Diego Union-Tribune, BBC News, Deutsche Welle

item.title: North County Homeowners Advised to Prevent Flooding Before Winter Rain
item.description:
Source: ABC 10News San Diego Original headline: How North County homeowners can protect against flooding before a rainy winter hits
North County homeowners are advised to prepare for potential flooding ahead of an expected rainy winter. Plumber Kenny Kniskern explains that newer homes typically use black plastic pipes joined with solvent weld, effective for clearing sewer blockages but vulnerable to tree roots. He warns that root intrusion can cause severe drainage issues, leading to hidden water damage. Kniskern emphasizes that standing water can seep into walls and insulation, fostering mold and bacterial growth, which may require full reconstruction. While newer homes in the area generally have more durable drainage systems, he urges residents to consult local plumbers to identify hidden risks. Kniskern notes that underground piping issues may not be visible until a storm event occurs, stressing the importance of proactive maintenance to prevent costly repairs.

item.title: Breakthrough vaccine for the deadliest skin cancer cut risk by almost half
item.description:
Source: Washington Post
A groundbreaking mRNA-based vaccine for melanoma reduced the risk of recurrence or death by 42% in a Phase 3 trial, according to Moderna and Merck. The treatment, intismeran autogene, uses personalized genetic data from a patient’s tumor to create a tailored vaccine, administered alongside immunotherapy. Karen Knudsen of the Parker Institute called the results 'well-conducted, meaningful,' while Moderna CEO Stéphane Bancel highlighted mRNA’s potential to transform cancer treatment. Side effects included fatigue and injection site pain. Data on overall survival was not yet available, though a 'favorable trend' was observed. The trial data was leaked before a planned Saturday presentation, causing Moderna’s stock to drop 25%. Researchers noted the vaccine’s personalized approach, using the same mRNA platform as COVID-19 vaccines. Melanoma, a deadly skin cancer with over 100,000 new cases annually in the U.S., remains a challenge even after surgery. Moderna and Merck are engaging with regulators for approval, though the FDA has no prior experience with this type of cancer vaccine. Trials for other mRNA-based vaccines in pancreatic, lung, and breast cancer are ongoing, with mixed results so far.
